paper_title: On the Ability of Neural Nets to Express Distributions
authors: Holden Lee, Rong Ge, Tengyu Ma, Andrej Risteski, Sanjeev Arora
statement: Note that this theorem gives a separation between Barron functions and compositions of Barron functions, and does not give a separation between distributions expressible by Barron functions and compositions of Barron functions. The analogous question for distributions is an open problem.
context: The condition 𝑛 ≡ 3 (mod 4) is not necessary; we include it only to avoid case analysis. Note that this theorem gives a separation between Barron functions and compositions of Barron functions, and does not give a separation between distributions expressible by Barron functions and compositions of Barron functions. The analogous question for distributions is an open problem. We will choose 𝑓 to be a certain radial function 𝑓 =R𝑓1 (‖𝑥‖) defined in Section 4.1.5 In order for 𝑓 to have large Barron constant, it is necessary for R𝑛 ‖𝜔‖2 |𝑓b(𝜔)| 𝑑𝜔 to be large, i.e. for 𝑓b to have significant mass far away from the origin. We ensure this holds by choosing 𝑓 to change sharply in the radial direction. This means 𝑓b has mass far away from the origin. Moreover, 𝑓b is radial because 𝑓 is radial, so 𝑓bRhas significant mass in a large shell. However, lower-bounding R𝑛 ‖𝜔‖2 |𝑓b(𝜔)| 𝑑𝜔 is not sufficient because the definition of the Barron constant requires us to bound this quantity over all extensions of 𝑓 .
